The principles that are to be borne in mind while considering an application for suspension of sentence after a finding of guilt has been arrived at by the trial court have been outlined by the Apex Court in Preet Pal Singh (supra), wherein it was held in paragraphs 35 and 38 as under:
35.
sentences._hearing_file: Xxxxx vs State Of Kerala on 8 January, 2025.json

sentences.text:
There is a difference between grant of bail under Section 439 CrPC in case of pre-trial arrest and suspension of sentence under Section 389 CrPC and grant of bail,
post conviction.
sentences._hearing_file: Xxxxx vs State Of Kerala on 8 January, 2025.json

sentences.text:
In the earlier case, there may be presumption of innocence, which is a fundamental postulate of criminal jurisprudence, and the courts may be liberal,
depending on the facts and circumstances of the case, on the principle that bail is the rule and jail is an exception, as held by this Court in Dataram Singh v. State of U.P.
[Dataram Singh v. State of U.P., [(2018) 3 SCC 22]

entities.text: Dataram Singh v. State of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Dataram Singh v. State of U.P., [(2018) 3 SCC 22]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences._hearing_file: Xxxxx vs State Of Kerala on 8 January, 2025.json

sentences.text: However, in case of post-conviction bail, by suspension of operation of the sentence, there is a finding of guilt and the question of presumption of innocence does not arise.
sentences._hearing_file: Xxxxx vs State Of Kerala on 8 January, 2025.json

sentences.text: Nor is the principle of bail being the rule and jail an exception attracted, once there is conviction upon trial.
sentences._hearing_file: Xxxxx vs State Of Kerala on 8 January, 2025.json

sentences.text: Rather, the court considering an application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail, is to consider the prima facie merits of the appeal, coupled with other factors.
sentences._hearing_file: Xxxxx vs State Of Kerala on 8 January, 2025.json

sentences.text:
There should be strong compelling reasons for grant of bail, notwithstanding an order of conviction,
by suspension of sentence, and this strong and compelling reason must be recorded in the order granting bail, as mandated in Section 389(1) CrPC.
xxxxxxx xxxxx   xxxx 38.
sentences._hearing_file: Xxxxx vs State Of Kerala on 8 January, 2025.json

sentences.text: In considering an application for suspension of sentence, the appellate court is only to examine if there is such patent infirmity in the order of conviction that renders the order of conviction prima facie erroneous.
sentences._hearing_file: Xxxxx vs State Of Kerala on 8 January, 2025.json

sentences.text: Where there is evidence that has been considered by the trial court, it is not open to a court considering application under Section 389 to reassess and/or re-analyse the same evidence and take a different view, to suspend the execution of the sentence and release the convict on bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Xxxxx vs State Of Kerala on 8 January, 2025.json

sentences.text: 7. Though the power to suspend an order of conviction, apart from the order of sentence, is not alien to Section 389(1) of the Code, its exercise should be limited to very exceptional cases.
sentences._hearing_file: Xxxxx vs State Of Kerala on 8 January, 2025.json

sentences.text: Merely because the convicted person files an appeal in challenge of the conviction, the court should not suspend the operation of the order of conviction.
sentences._hearing_file: Xxxxx vs State Of Kerala on 8 January, 2025.json

sentences.text: The court has a duty to look at all aspects including the ramifications of keeping such conviction in abeyance.

sentences.text: 8. Having considered the materials, we find that the innocent child who was a victim of brutal sexual abuse by the appellant disclosed to her PT teacher about the devious predatory acts of the appellant.

sentences.text: Evidence reveals that the child had intimated to her father about the sexual abuse to which she was subjected to, but the father, keeping the future of the child in mind, failed to report the matter to the police.

sentences.text: The discrepancies pointed out by the learned counsel pale into insignificance when faced with the overwhelming evidence let in by the prosecution to prove the case of sexual abuse on a minor girl child under 10 years of age.

sentences.text:
We find,
prima facie, that the learned Sessions Judge has evaluated the evidence in a proper and careful manner while arriving at the finding of guilt.
sentences._hearing_file: Xxxxx vs State Of Kerala on 8 January, 2025.json

sentences.text: We find no patent infirmity in the order of conviction as forcefully contended by the learned counsel appearing for the appellant.
sentences._hearing_file: Xxxxx vs State Of Kerala on 8 January, 2025.json

sentences.text: 9. We are therefore of the considered opinion that the appellant has not made out any strong or compelling reasons for suspending the execution of the sentence.

sentences.text: This application is dismissed.

After relying upon various precedents, in paragraph 26 this court held that:
(1) Unless the criminal proceedings are terminated by quashing the same, there will be utter chaos, confusion and even havoc in the life of the victim who married the accused, and who is leading a happy life.
